To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the solution structure of a new phosphoprotein recognition domain, the FHA2 of yeast checkpoint protein Rad53, has been determined.
the FHA2 domain of Rad53 recognizes pTyr-containing Rad9 peptides and that this recognition involves a conserved surface of the FHA domain.
the structure of a new phospho-peptide-binding domain containing FHA2 of Rad 53 was determined by NMR spectroscopy and that the binding of the domain with phosphorylated Rad9 peptide was confirmed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure-function of a new domain containing the second FHA of Rad53.
a new phosphopeptides-binding domain containing the yeast Rad53 FHA2, and the structure-function of this module is discussed.
the structure and function of a phosphopeptide-binding module, the FHA domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the FHA2 domain is similar to the structure of the previously described FHA1 domain, but that the binding specificity is different.
FHA2 recognizes phosphorylated Rad53.
the FHA domain has a conserved structure, which binds to a conserved phosphopeptide binding site, but the specificity of the binding is variable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FHA2-containing domain has a beta-sandwish structure, binds pTyr-containing peptides, and is a new phosphopeptides-binding domain.
FHA domains are structurally similar, and that the ligand of the FHA domain is a pTyr or a pSer/Thr residue.
FHA2 of Rad 53 is a novel type of phosphopeptide-binding module.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FHA domains are structurally similar, but not identical to phosphotyrosine binding (PTB) domains.
FHA2-containing domains could be a new family of phosphopeptide-binding domains.

FHA2 of Rad9 can recognize pTyr and the phosphorylated peptide from Rad9 and that the FHA2 domain is structurally related to the FHA domain of the human protein kinase Raf1, which has previously been shown to interact with pSer-containing peptides.
